raw_response:
Well, sit down, let me think about it.

My 9 mu — I've split it the way I always do. About 6 mu for wheat-maize, the double crop, on the better land near the road. The other 3 mu, the lower piece by the ditch, I keep in cotton. Always been cotton there. My father grew cotton on that plot. The soil is a bit saltier and wheat doesn't do as well there.

I'm 72. My back isn't what it was. My son works in Handan at a factory, comes back for the wheat harvest and maize planting week — that's the busy time, you can't manage otherwise, only 5 or 6 days between combining wheat and getting maize in. My wife helps with the cotton picking but slowly. Honestly, I've thought about giving up cotton — too much bending, too much spraying — but the price last year wasn't bad and the cotton buyer still comes to the village. One more year, we'll see.

**Wheat (6 mu).** I plant around October 10, same as always, after the maize comes off. I use seed I bought from the agricultural supply shop — Jimai 22 or whatever they have, about 15 kg/mu broadcast. Before sowing I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the 15-15-15 kind, 40 kg — that's the base. My neighbor Old Wang uses more but I can't afford it every year. In spring when the wheat starts jointing and I see it turning a bit yellow, I topdress urea, about 15 kg per mu. I irrigate three times: once in winter to settle it, once at jointing together with the urea, once at heading if it hasn't rained. Each irrigation costs money — the pump uses electricity and you pay by the hour. If the spring rain comes, I skip one. I expect maybe 400 kg/mu. Last year I got 380, the year before 420. Depends on the weather.

**Maize (6 mu).** Right after wheat harvest, middle of June, my son comes home and we rent the neighbor's seed drill for half a day. Hybrid seed from the shop, Zhengdan 958 type, about 4 kg/mu. The drill puts compound fertilizer down with the seed — 30 kg/mu of the 15-15-15. Then at the big trumpet stage, end of July, I topdress about 15 kg urea per mu by hand. Usually I only irrigate once if July is dry — maize doesn't need as much water as wheat. I spray herbicide early on, and if armyworm shows up I spray once. Expect about 450 kg/mu, sell most of it.

**Cotton (3 mu).** This is the hard one. Plant mid-late April, I use plastic mulch — buy the film and the planter comes for hire, 30 yuan/mu. Seed is about 2 kg/mu, coated seed from the shop. I put compound fertilizer down before laying the mulch, about 40 kg/mu, and topdress urea around flowering, 10 kg. Cotton needs spraying — aphids, bollworm, sometimes spider mites — I spray 4 or 5 times through the summer, it adds up. Irrigate once or twice from the well. Picking starts in September, goes into October, three or four rounds. My wife and I pick together, slowly. Maybe a little help from my daughter-in-law if she comes. I expect maybe 230 kg/mu of lint — not great, but it's always been that piece of ground.

I haven't changed much in years. Why would I? The ones who try new things — some get rich, most don't. I know what my land gives me.
